_comment: Regauntless canonical bestiary. The game's Monster Manual as DATA (datastream, not prose). Read by the crawl-sim now, by the game later. PROCESS: we are DATAMINING the SRD — EVERY creature gets its full stat block ('srd' block) pulled and saved verbatim, regardless of CR or whether it fights. CR and 'archetype:noncombat' are CLASSIFICATION METADATA on the data, NOT a skip filter (scope is a moving line — a noncombat housecat may become a boss; an out-of-scope CR may come in-scope). 'archetype'/'behavior'/'notes*' are OUR definitions (how it plays in 2D + how the sim models it). Grown creature-by-creature via the pull->full-srd->interpret-or-mark->append walkthrough. See .kiro/steering/combat-model.md.

_schema.name: string
_schema.notes2D: string (how it plays on the hex field)
_schema.notesSim: string (how the numbers-sim models it; note any spatial-skill->probability abstraction)

monsters.name: Kobold

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size monster (the 1st-level Warrior sample).
srd.ac: 15 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +1 natural, +2 leather), touch 12, flat-footed 14
srd.skills: Craft (trapmaking) +2, Hide +6, Listen +2, Move Silently +2, Profession (miner) +2, Search +2, Spot +2
srd.organization: Gang (4-9), band (10-100 plus 100% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults and 1 leader of 4th-6th level), warband (10-24 plus 2-4 dire weasels), tribe (40-400 plus sergeants, 1-2 lieutenants of 4th-5th, 1 leader of 6th-8th, and 5-8 dire weasels)
srd.flavor: Kobolds are short, reptilian humanoids with cowardly and sadistic tendencies. Scaly skin from dark rusty brown to rusty black; glowing red eyes; nonprehensile tail. Wear ragged clothing favoring red and orange. 2 to 2-1/2 feet tall, 35-45 lb. Speak Draconic with a voice like a yapping dog.
srd.combat: Kobolds like to attack with overwhelming odds (at least 2:1) or trickery; below that they usually flee. They attack gnomes on sight at equal numbers. They begin a fight by slinging bullets, closing only when foes are weakened. Whenever they can, kobolds set up ambushes near trapped areas.
srd.lightSensitivity: Ex: dazzled in bright sunlight or within a daylight spell.
srd.skillsText: +2 racial on Craft (trapmaking), Profession (miner), Search. Warrior sample pre-racial scores: Str 13, Dex 11, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 8.
srd.crText: Kobolds with NPC class levels have CR = character level -3.

specials: Darkvision 60ft
Light Sensitivity (dazzled in bright light / daylight)

priorityList: if LoS && has-shot -> fire sling (flat)
else no LoS -> move to gain sightline / maintain range (kite)
else -> weak spear melee if cornered

monsters.notes2D: Gauntlet 'Lobber' feel but with a FLAT shot (sling), not an arc. Holds range, plinks via LoS, kites when closed on; its 'cowardice/flee' IS the kiting. Fragile (4hp, ~1hit). Light Sensitivity = possible interaction with lit-from-below light-wells (parked).
monsters.notesSim: 4hp unit, flat ranged ~1 dmg (1d3-1), speed 6 hexes/rd. Kiting/dodge is positional -> abstract to a probability in the numbers-sim. Dies to ~any hero shot.

monsters.name: Goblin

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size monster (the 1st-level Warrior sample).
srd.ac: 15 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +2 leather armor, +1 light shield), touch 12, flat-footed 14
srd.skills: Hide +5, Listen +2, Move Silently +5, Ride +4, Spot +2
srd.organization: Gang (4-9), band (10-100 plus 100% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults and 1 leader of 4th-6th level), warband (10-24 with worg mounts), tribe (40-400 plus noncombatants, sergeants, 1-2 lieutenants of 4th-5th, 1 leader of 6th-8th, 10-24 worgs, 2-4 dire wolves)
srd.flavor: A goblin stands 3 to 3-1/2 feet tall, 40-45 lb. Eyes dull and glazed, red to yellow. Skin yellow through orange to deep red (a tribe is usually one color). Wear dark drab soiled leather. Speak Goblin; Int 12+ also speak Common. Most encountered outside their homes are 1st-level warriors.
srd.combat: Being bullied by bigger, stronger creatures has taught goblins to exploit their few advantages: sheer numbers and malicious ingenuity. A fair fight is meaningless to them; they favor ambushes, overwhelming odds, and dirty tricks. Poor at strategy and cowardly by nature, they tend to flee if a battle turns against them. With proper supervision they can implement complex plans, and then their numbers become a deadly advantage.
srd.skillsText: +4 racial on Move Silently and Ride. Worg-mounted cavalry usually take Mounted Combat in place of Alertness (reduces Spot/Listen +3 to +1).
srd.crText: Goblins with NPC class levels have CR = character level -2.

specials: Darkvision 60ft

priorityList: if LoS && has-shot -> throw javelin (flat)
else no LoS -> move to close/gain sightline
else -> morningstar melee on contact

monsters.notes2D: The 'upward variation' from the ghost/kobold: a real little soldier. Closes to melee (morningstar) but will throw javelins (flat shot) with LoS. Survives contact (not a detonator) -> brawler-ish, but weak (5hp). Flees when a battle turns (tactical AI -> optional for auto-crawler).
monsters.notesSim: 5hp, AC15, melee 1d6 / ranged 1d4, speed 6 hexes/rd, +1 BAB. Fights back at contact (multi-round melee if it survives). Flat-shot firing discipline applies (holds if friendly/spawner blocks lane).

monsters.name: Badger

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Two columns: normal Badger + Celestial Badger (CR 1/2 both).

variants.specialQualities: Low-light vision, scent, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to acid 5/cold 5/electricity 5, spell resistance 6

srd.flavor: The badger is a furry animal with a squat, powerful body. Its strong forelimbs are armed with long claws for digging. An adult is 2 to 3 feet long and weighs 25-35 lb.
srd.combat: Badgers attack with their sharp claws and teeth.
srd.rage: Ex: A badger that takes damage in combat flies into a berserk rage on its next turn, clawing and biting madly until either it or its opponent is dead. +4 Str, +4 Con, -2 AC. Cannot end its rage voluntarily.
srd.celestial: Celestial badgers are commonly summoned by summon monster I. Smite Evil (Su): once/day a normal melee attack deals +1 damage vs an evil foe.

specials: Low-light vision
Scent (always knows player location; LoS irrelevant)
Burrow 10ft (alternate movement — OFF the hex-lane plane; untargetable by lane-shots while underground)
Rage (Ex): on taking damage, next turn berserks until it or its foe is dead: +4 Str, +4 Con, -2 AC, CANNOT end voluntarily -> never flees

priorityList: SCENT: always knows player pos, ignore LoS; move STRAIGHT toward player (INT 2, no clever pathing)
if a wall blocks the straight line -> burrow through/past it (don't path around)
at 3 hexes from player -> BURROW: dive (untargetable), spend remaining movement repositioning UNDERGROUND toward a free hex adjacent to the player
next round -> SURFACE for free (no AP cost) + full attack (2 claws + bite)
on contact: 3 attacks/turn; if damaged -> RAGE (buffed, reckless, fights to death)

monsters.notes2D: Relentless burrowing bruiser. Scent = can't juke it (ignores LoS, always comes straight). Digs through walls (cover useless). Burrow-closer is a 2-ROUND tell: at 3 hexes it dives (untargetable) + tunnels under a free adjacent hex; NEXT round surfaces free and mauls. Counter is PURELY out-DPS during the approach window (before the 3-hex burrow) — no juking, no cover, no LoS tricks. Harder than a ghost: walls don't help. Denying free adjacent exit hexes (corner/crowd) limits where it erupts. Underground = a shadow/bulge under the lit-from-below floor (telegraph; parked).
monsters.notesSim: 6hp, AC15, 3 melee attacks/turn (2x +4 1d2-1, bite -1 1d3-1), speed 6 hexes/rd, burrow 2 hexes/rd. Models: LoS-independent straight approach; at dist<=3 goes untargetable 1 round then guaranteed-contacts next round. Rage = damage-triggered buff state. FIRST multi-attack-per-turn creature (validates attacks-from-AP) and FIRST off-plane movement (burrow -> untargetable window).

monsters.name: Bat

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size. Evaluated and EXCLUDED as a threat (no attack) — archived for completeness.
srd.flavor: Bats are nocturnal flying mammals. The statistics presented here describe small, insectivorous bats.
srd.blindsense: Ex: A bat notices and locates creatures within 20 feet. Opponents still have 100% concealment against a creature with blindsense.
srd.skillsText: *+4 racial on Spot and Listen; lost if blindsense is negated.

monsters.notes2D: NONCOMBAT — no attack (1 hp, flies). Not a threat mob; excluded from the enemy roster. Recorded so it reads as evaluated-and-excluded, not an oversight. (Could exist later as ambient fauna/decoration — poppable flavor — but is NOT a spawner threat.)

monsters.name: Cat

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size. Evaluated and EXCLUDED as a threat (housecat) — archived for completeness.
srd.skills: Balance +10, Climb +6, Hide +16*, Jump +10, Listen +3, Move Silently +8, Spot +3
srd.flavor: The statistics presented here describe a common housecat.
srd.combat: Cats prefer to sneak up on their prey.
srd.skillsText: +4 racial on Climb, Hide, Move Silently; +8 racial on Jump; +8 racial on Balance. Use Dex instead of Str for Climb and Jump. *In tall grass or heavy undergrowth the Hide bonus rises to +8.

monsters.notes2D: NOT A MONSTER — a housecat. Technically attacks (2 claws 1d2-4, bite 1d3-4 = ~1 dmg) but 2 hp and negligible; fauna, not a threat. Same natural-attack brawler profile as the Badger but strictly weaker — introduces NO new mechanic. Excluded from the enemy roster (fauna only).

monsters.name: Monstrous Centipede
monsters.cr: varies by size (in-scope: Tiny 1/8, Small 1/4, Medium 1/2)

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block, FULL page. All sizes + Fiendish column + poison-by-size table + flavor captured whole so scope can expand with no re-fetch. We only INTERPRET Tiny/Small/Medium right now.
srd.flavor: Monstrous centipedes tend to attack anything that resembles food, biting with their jaws and injecting their poison.

sizeTable.specialQualities: Darkvision 60 ft, resistance to cold 5 and fire 5, spell resistance 6, vermin traits
Darkvision 60 ft, resistance to cold 5 and fire 5, spell resistance 8, vermin traits
DR 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to cold 5 and fire 5, spell resistance 11, vermin traits
DR 10/magic, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to cold 10 and fire 10, spell resistance 17, vermin traits
DR 10/magic, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to cold 10 and fire 10, spell resistance 25, vermin traits

poison.text: A monstrous centipede has a poisonous bite. The details vary by the centipede's size, as shown on the table. The save DCs are Constitution-based. The indicated damage is both initial and secondary damage.

fiendish.smiteGoodText: Once per day a fiendish monstrous centipede can make a normal melee attack to deal extra damage (= its HD, max as table) against a good foe.
fiendish.summonedBy: summon monster I (medium), II (large), III (huge), VI (gargantuan), VIII (colossal)
fiendish.note: Huge+ natural weapons treated as magic for overcoming DR.

srd.skillsText: Monstrous centipedes have a +4 racial bonus on Spot, and +8 on Climb and Hide. Use Str or Dex (whichever higher) for Climb. Can take 10 on Climb even if threatened/distracted.

monsters._interpretedScope: Tiny (1/8), Small (1/4), Medium (1/2) — the CR<1 slice. Large+ and all Fiendish captured verbatim above but NOT interpreted yet.

abilities.note: Dex 15 / Con 10 across in-scope sizes; Str scales 1/5/9 (Tiny/Small/Medium); Int Ø (mindless vermin)

specials: Darkvision 60ft
Vermin traits (mindless: immune to mind-affecting; no clever pathing)
Poison bite (first STATUS-EFFECT mechanic — see behavior.statusEffect)

priorityList: MINDLESS (Int Ø): move STRAIGHT toward nearest non-vermin (no pathing, no LoS logic) — attack anything that resembles food
on contact -> bite + apply poison
climber: can traverse walls (climb speed = land speed) — reaches over cover

statusEffect.name: poison
statusEffect.srd: Fort save or take Dex damage, initial AND secondary (hits twice unless saved)
statusEffect.mapping: RESOLVED (Mids house-rule — SRD Dex-damage has no analog in our statless hero, so we define the FEEL): poison is a PER-AVATAR, NON-DAMAGE status FLAG (sticks to the bitten hero, NOT the shared pool). Follows the general on-hit status shape {baseEffect, overflowEffect, selfCure} — see combat-model.md 'Status effects'.
statusEffect.baseEffect: flag OFF->ON: -10 ft / -2 hexes movement speed while poisoned. Binary, NOT additive.
statusEffect.overflowEffect: re-hit while already ON: micro-stun (brief AP/tick loss) — a swarm of centipedes can chain-stun a poisoned hero. Not a deeper slow.
statusEffect.selfCure: ~40s default (FEEL knob; stored internally as rounds/ticks so it survives tick-rate changes & the numbers-sim can use it). Each new bite REFRESHES the timer -> stays on through the fight + a little spillover, then clears on its own.
statusEffect.simNote: sim thinks in rounds: express ~40s as N rounds at normal pace. Model = per-hero bool + refresh-on-rehit + the -2hex move penalty; micro-stun = lose some AP on a re-hit round.

monsters.notes2D: First VENOMOUS mob + first STATUS-EFFECT delivery. Mindless vermin (Int Ø) = dead-simple AI: straight-line approach, bite, done — no kiting, no LoS logic. Damage is trivial (Str penalty -> ~1/bite); the THREAT is the poison, not the hit. Climb speed = reaches over/around cover (walls less useful vs it). Colony/swarm organization (Tiny 8-16) = spawner CHAFF that's dangerous by poison + chain MICRO-STUN (base slow then overflow stun), not per-hit damage. SIZE LADDER (Tiny->Small->Medium->...) is the SRD's own scaling curve — a clean source for 'level scales the monster' using one archetype.
monsters.notesSim: In-scope: 1/2/4 hp, AC14, single bite/round (low/no damage) + poison-on-hit. Models: mindless straight approach (no LoS gate); on contact roll bite, on hit apply poison (Fort DC 10 vs hero). Poison EFFECT depends on Mids' mapping decision (slow debuff vs pool-DoT) — sim can't model it until that's set. Swarm = many cheap units; validates contact-phase + status stacking. Poison save math: hero Fort vs fixed DC 10.

monsters.name: Dog

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Two columns: normal Dog + Celestial Dog (CR 1/3 both). Also covers coyotes/jackals/African wild dogs.

variants.specialQualities: Low-light vision, scent, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to acid 5/cold 5/electricity 5, spell resistance 6

srd.flavor: The statistics describe a fairly small dog of about 20 to 50 pounds. Also usable for small wild canines such as coyotes, jackals, and African wild dogs.
srd.combat: Dogs generally hunt in packs, chasing and exhausting prey until they can drag it down.
srd.skillsText: +4 racial on Jump. *+4 racial on Survival when tracking by scent.
srd.celestial: Celestial dogs are commonly summoned by summon monster I. Smite Evil (Su): once/day a normal melee attack deals +1 damage vs an evil foe.

specials: Low-light vision
Scent (always knows player location; LoS-independent — vector always live, see combat-model.md 'Sensing')

priorityList: SCENT: always-live vector straight toward player (no LoS gate); inherits the DEFAULT mob-movement model (combat-model.md): collision-slide-drain, NO pathfinding
on contact -> bite (single attack, 1d4+1)
behavior.movementModel: DEFAULT (combat-model.md 'Mob movement'): desired vector = straight at player; collide-and-slide vs walls+bodies; pile & drain; jaggies self-fill. No special movement — the dog is the straightforward FAST brawler that simply inherits the shared rule. Faster drain than most (8 hexes/round) so it surges to the front of a mixed pile (speed-sorting).

monsters.notes2D: The straightforward FAST pack-brawler — the 'honest' creature with no gimmick. vs Badger (same 6hp/scent/CR-ish): simpler (single bite, no burrow, no rage) but FASTER (40ft/8 hexes vs 30/6) and PACKS (5-12). Scent = LoS-independent (always-live vector, can't juke by breaking LoS) but honest about it — no untargetable window, just runs at you fast, in numbers. Whole threat profile = SPEED + NUMBERS, not a special. Anchors the 'fast rusher' end of the brawler axis (vs the slow-tanky brawler). In a mixed spawn, speed-sorts to the FRONT of the pile. Obvious pet/familiar (hound companion) candidate later, but recorded as a real melee threat.
monsters.notesSim: 6hp, AC15, single bite +2 (1d4+1), speed 8 hexes/round (FAST). Models: always-live straight approach (scent, no LoS gate); on contact single melee attack. No multi-attack (unlike badger), no status (unlike centipede), no ranged (unlike goblin). Validates: fast-closer in the approach-race (8 hexes closes the fire-rate-vs-movement gap quicker) and speed-sorting in a mixed pile. First creature whose lift is purely movement-speed + pack-count.

monsters.name: Donkey

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size. Also describes burros.
srd.flavor: These long-eared, horselike creatures are surefooted and sturdy. The statistics could also describe burros.
srd.combat: A donkey bites only when it has no way to escape.
srd.carryingCapacity: Light up to 50 lb; medium 51-100; heavy 101-150. Can drag 750 lb.

monsters.notes2D: NONCOMBAT — beast of burden. Technically bites (1d2) but SRD says it 'bites only when it has no way to escape' — it flees, doesn't fight. Solitary, not a threat mob; excluded from the enemy roster. No new mechanic (scent + bite already covered). Reserved for mount/pack-animal flavor. Part of the SRD 'livestock cluster' (donkey/mule/horse/pony/camel) — mostly noncombat or out-of-scope beasts of burden.

monsters.name: Mule

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size. Sterile donkey x horse crossbreed.
srd.flavor: Mules are sterile crossbreeds of donkeys and horses. Similar to a light horse, slightly stronger and more agile.
srd.combat: A mule's powerful kick can be dangerous.
srd.carryingCapacity: Light up to 230 lb; medium 231-460; heavy 461-690. Can drag 3,450 lb.
srd.skillsText: +2 racial on Dex checks to avoid slipping/falling.

monsters.notes2D: OUT OF CURRENT COMBAT SCOPE (CR 1, boundary) + beast of burden. Domesticated, 2-hoof kick (1d4+3) — more capable than the donkey but still livestock, not a spawner threat. Data saved verbatim for the datamine (scope is a moving line); marked noncombat/out-of-scope. Part of the livestock cluster. Reserved for mount/pack-animal flavor.

monsters.name: Eagle

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size (describes any similar diurnal bird of prey).
srd.flavor: Birds of prey inhabiting nearly every terrain; prefer high, secluded nesting spots. ~3 ft long, ~7 ft wingspan. Describes any similar-sized diurnal bird of prey.
srd.combat: Eagles dive at prey, raking with their powerful talons.

specials: Low-light vision
FLIGHT (fly 80ft, average) — off-ground movement; see notesSim for sim/2D handling of fliers

priorityList: FLIER: fly fast (80ft/16 hexes) toward target; dive to contact
on contact: full attack (2 talons + bite)
inherits DEFAULT movement model, but in 3 dimensions (flight) — see open 'fliers' question
behavior.movementModel: DEFAULT collision-slide-drain, EXCEPT airborne: flies OVER ground obstacles/bodies (doesn't pile with ground mobs). FIRST FLIER — raises an open design question (how do fliers interact with the 2-grid floor/wall model, LoS over cover, can ground shots hit them). PARKED — spatial, Mids-owned.

monsters.notes2D: FIRST FLIER. Fast (80ft = 16 hexes/round airborne) multi-attack diver (2 talons + bite, like the badger's 3-attack profile). Flight is the new axis: flies over ground piles/cover, doesn't queue with ground mobs, dives onto the party. Opens design Qs (parked, spatial/Mids): do fliers occupy the same hex grid? can they be blocked/shot by ground units? do they ignore the collision-slide pile entirely? LoS over walls? Mechanically otherwise a vanilla fast multi-attack brawler.
monsters.notesSim: 5hp, AC14, 3 attacks/turn (2x talon +3 1d4, bite -2 1d4), fly 16 hexes/round. Models as a fast multi-attack brawler; FLIGHT abstracted for now (sim has no z-axis) — flag: fliers may ignore ground-collision piles and close unobstructed. Real flier rules (grid interaction, shootability) TBD with Mids.

monsters.name: Toad

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size. NO attack.
srd.flavor: These diminutive amphibians are innocuous and beneficial, since they eat insects.

monsters.notes2D: NONCOMBAT — no attack (1 hp). 'Innocuous and beneficial.' Not a threat mob; excluded from the enemy roster. Data saved for the datamine. Reserved for ambient fauna / familiar flavor (classic witch's toad). Same bucket as Bat.

monsters.name: Owl

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Two columns: Owl + Celestial Owl (CR 1/4 both). Combines both talons into a single attack.

variants.specialQualities: Low-light vision, darkvision 60 ft, resistance to acid 5/cold 5/electricity 5, spell resistance 6

srd.flavor: Nocturnal birds of prey 1 to 2 feet long, wingspans up to 6 feet. They combine both talons into a single attack.
srd.combat: Owls swoop quietly down onto prey, attacking with their powerful talons.
srd.skillsText: +8 racial on Listen, +14 on Move Silently. *+8 racial on Spot in shadowy illumination.
srd.celestial: Summoned by summon monster I. Smite Evil (Su): once/day +1 damage vs evil foe.

specials: Low-light vision
FLIGHT (fly 40ft, average) — see Eagle notes + parked fliers question

priorityList: FLIER: fly toward target, swoop to contact
on contact: single talon attack (trivial dmg)
inherits flier handling (see Eagle / parked fliers question)
behavior.movementModel: Flier (see Eagle). Slower than eagle (40ft/8 hexes airborne), single weak attack.

monsters.notes2D: Eagle-lite: smaller, slower flier (40ft/8 hexes), SINGLE combined-talon attack for trivial damage (1d4-3, Str 4). High AC (17) for its tier (Dex 17 + size + natural) so it's annoyingly evasive but barely hurts. Stealthy (Move Silently +17 — swoops quietly). Solitary. Obvious familiar candidate (wizard's owl). Same flier questions as Eagle (parked). Mechanically the weakest flier — almost a noncombat, but it does attack so recorded as a (weak) brawler.
monsters.notesSim: 4hp, AC17, single talon +5 (1d4-3 ~ often 1), fly 8 hexes/round. High AC = whiffs more hero shots than its tier suggests; near-zero damage output. Flight abstracted (see Eagle). Validates a high-evasion low-damage flier.

monsters.name: Weasel

srd._note: Verbatim SRD 3.5 stat block + flavor, full page. Single-size (also applies to ferrets). Carries ATTACH -> our Latcher archetype.
srd.skills: Balance +12, Climb +10, Escape Artist +4, Hide +11, Move Silently +8, Spot +3
srd.flavor: These little mammals are aggressive predators but usually confine themselves to smaller prey. Also applies to ferrets.
srd.attach: Ex: If a weasel hits with a bite, it latches on with its jaws and automatically deals bite damage each round it remains attached. An attached weasel loses its Dex bonus to AC (AC 12), and can be struck or grappled. To remove it, the opponent must achieve a pin.
srd.skillsText: +4 racial Move Silently, +8 racial Balance & Climb. Uses Dex for Climb. Can always take 10 on Climb even if rushed/threatened.

specials: Low-light vision
Scent
Climb 20ft
Attach (Ex) — FIRST LATCHER mechanic; see combat-model.md 'Latcher / Attach archetype'

priorityList: NOT spawner-fed: hand-placed in clumps of 3-5, a few per dungeon (ambient ambush pocket)
fast rusher: bolt at a hero, jump on (bite -> ATTACH)
while attached: ride + auto-tick per the hands-capacity ladder (combat-model.md); removed only by an ALLY (shot / conjured-hand / AoE repel)

latcher.capacity: hero HANDS (default 2, per-hero stat) manage latchers; overflow bites freely

ladderByCount.1: Distract (defensive debuff: take MORE incoming — SRD lost-Dex-to-AC)

latcher.removal: ally's shot scrapes off / Bigby-style conjured-hand plucks / AoE fumigate-repel. CASTER EXCEPTION: anti-latcher spells are Verbal-only/Focus (NO somatic) -> a caster self-casts out even with full hands (hands-independent); the 'can't self-clear' rule is MARTIAL-specific, caster = weasel-insurance. ENVIRONMENT: route to a water tile (wash/drown off) or vent/gas tile (environmental fumigate) -> map-as-participant, per-latcher-type, a few specific cases (ties to cell/hazard system).
latcher.danger: CONTEXTUAL — trivial alone; lethal stacked during a wave (Distract amplifies all other incoming)
latcher.openKnobs: does the ally scrape-shot HURT the ridden hero (rough) or clean-remove? ; default hands value

monsters.notes2D: FIRST LATCHER. A 2hp weasel whose stats are nothing but whose MECHANIC is a whole enemy class: fast rush, jump on, RIDE. Attach = persistent on-hero state (first non-positional contact). Hand-placed clumps of 3-5 (not spawner chaff) = ambush pockets that EXCEED your 2 hands to force the DoT/leg-slow overflow. Inverse of the ghost (fast closer, but sticks-and-drains vs burst-and-gone). Whole point = FORCED CO-OP: hands full -> a teammate must clean you (shot / conjured-hand / AoE repel). Climber (reaches over cover). Obvious whimsy: 'get it off me!' Also the demand-creator for future removal spells.
monsters.notesSim: 2hp, AC14 (12 while attached — easier to kill once on), bite +4 (1d3-4). Models: fast approach, on-hit sets ATTACHED state on that hero; thereafter auto-tick the hands-capacity ladder (distract/slow/DoT/slow/slow by attached-count) until an ally removes it. Validates: persistent per-avatar on-hero state, hands-capacity primitive, forced-co-op removal, contextual danger (debuff amplifies concurrent wave damage). Attached-AC drop = reward for committing (it's squishier once riding).
